claims.title: Exact weighted Báez-Duarte rate: κ(σ) = 2(σ − Θ)
claims.class: novo (proposal R105, ShantiDraconis/M-Core issue #176, opened 2026-10-27, approved 2026-11-05)

claims.meaning: For the weighted Báez-Duarte distance D_N(σ) and Θ = sup Re ρ, the best polynomial rate exponent is exactly 2(σ − Θ) on (Θ, 1); the open question Q2(iii) (PisoPonderado, declared OPEN_MATH in round 76) is a theorem; RH holds iff D_N(σ₀) has rate 2σ₀ − 1 at one fixed σ₀ ∈ (½, 1).

claims.meaning: For an abstract class of L-functions closed under products (with 1/L = Σ μ(n)n^{-s}), a rate κ of the Báez-Duarte distance on a good line Re s = σ forces L ≠ 0 on Re s > σ − κ/2; one rate for the product certifies the zero-free region of every factor (ζ·L(s,χ) under a named good-line hypothesis for L(s,χ)). Decides neither RH nor GRH.

claims.title: Riemann hypothesis numerically verified up to height 3 000 209 302 471.5
claims.class: numerical verification (rigorous interval arithmetic), above the published record of Platt–Trudgian (2021)
claims.claim: All nontrivial zeros of ζ with 0 < Im s ≤ 3 000 209 302 471.5 lie on Re s = ½. Below T_PT = 3 000 175 332 800 this is Platt–Trudgian (2021); the range (T_PT, 3 000 209 302 471.5] is new here: 33 969 671.5 units of height, 145 389 043 zeros, deficit 0 in every gluing, N(3 000 209 302 471.5) = 12 363 298 826 181.
claims.method: FLINT 3 / Arb, 256-bit interval arithmetic; Turing's method for N(T) (acb_dirichlet_zeta_nzeros); bands of 120 000 units glued with N(b) of one band equal to N(a) of the next, computed by independent jobs; GitHub Actions runs listed in VALORES_FIXADOS.md (first run above the record: 41559243734, 2026-11-03; last: 43344579894, 2026-11-13).
